title: Merge two contact lists and remove the unsubscribed
examObjective: Predicting the result of core DataWeave functions
basics: `++` joins two Arrays into one. `--` removes from the left Array every element that appears in the right Array. `-` removes a single value: `[1, 2, 3] - 2` is `[1, 3]`.
prompt:
Marketing combines the CRM contacts and the web-shop contacts into one send list, `payload.crm` followed by `payload.shop`. Duplicates are fine at this stage; another step removes them.

Anyone in `payload.unsubscribed` must not receive the mail, however many times they appear in the two lists.
hints: Join the lists, then remove. Which operator removes a whole list of values?
The second hidden case has the same unsubscribed address in both lists. Removing it from one list only is not enough.
`(a ++ b) -- c` removes every occurrence of every element of `c`.

mustFail.why: removes the unsubscribed only from the CRM list, so the same person still arrives from the shop list
removes only the first unsubscribed address with -, so a second unsubscribed address stays

explanation.approach: Join first, then remove, so the removal sees every copy. `--` removes all occurrences of every value in its right-hand Array. `-` removes one value, all occurrences of it.

snippets.label: - with a list removes the list as one value
snippets.note: Nothing matches the Array ["a"] as a whole, so nothing is removed.
